Pentaho Server: The central web application that hosts and runs Pentaho's analytics and data-integration services. It bundles the BI Server, Data Integration Server, Pentaho User Console, security, and the content repository, and in version 11 ships on Tomcat 10.
Archive installation: A deployment method that installs Pentaho 11 from a downloaded ZIP archive that already bundles Tomcat 10, giving a faster, opinionated setup than wiring Pentaho into your own application server. This course uses the archive approach on Ubuntu Linux.
PDI: Pentaho Data Integration, also known as Kettle, the ETL engine for extracting, transforming, and loading data into databases, warehouses, and applications. It is one of the two halves of the Pentaho 11 release.
PBA: Pentaho Business Analytics, the reporting, dashboarding, and analysis half of the suite. It ships on the same release cadence as PDI in Pentaho 11.
Spoon: The desktop graphical client for designing and testing PDI jobs and transformations. In version 11 it is positioned as the legacy tool, with Pipeline Designer offered as the browser-based successor.
Pentaho User Console: The web UI, abbreviated PUC, for creating, browsing, scheduling, and viewing Pentaho content. Pentaho 11 introduces a redesigned modern PUC alongside the classic interface.
Pipeline Designer: A browser-based tool introduced in Pentaho 11 for authoring ETL transformations and jobs without the Spoon desktop client. It remains compatible with content created in Spoon.
Carte: A lightweight Jetty-based web server for remote execution, monitoring, and clustering of PDI transformations and jobs. It exposes a REST API and is useful for scaling ETL across multiple machines.
Pan: The command-line tool that runs a PDI transformation (a .ktr file) from a shell or scheduler, without opening Spoon.
Kitchen: The command-line tool that runs a PDI job (a .kjb file) from a shell or scheduler. It is the job-running sibling of Pan.
Transformation: A PDI data-flow of steps connected by hops, stored in a .ktr file, that moves and reshapes rows of data.
Job: A PDI orchestration unit, stored in a .kjb file, that sequences transformations and other tasks with control flow and conditions.
Repository: The central store the Pentaho Server uses for reports, dashboards, ETL assets, and metadata. It is backed by a supported relational database such as PostgreSQL.
Jackrabbit: The Apache Jackrabbit JCR content repository that holds Pentaho solutions, security data, and content metadata, persisted into the configured relational database. The Repository Browser connects to this store.
Quartz: The scheduler component whose data lives in its own database in the Pentaho Repository. It drives scheduled execution of jobs and transformations on the server.
Hibernate: The persistence layer used for audit logging in the Pentaho Repository, configured via hibernate-settings.xml to point at the PostgreSQL configuration.
Operations Mart: A set of database tables and scripts that capture usage and performance data so administrators can report on how the Pentaho system is being used.
PostgreSQL: The relational database recommended and used by default in this course to back the Pentaho Repository. Pentaho 11 supports versions 15 and 17, with the labs installing PostgreSQL 17 plus pgAdmin 4.
pg_hba.conf: The PostgreSQL host-based authentication file that controls who may connect and how they authenticate. The labs configure it to use password authentication such as scram-sha-256 or md5.
JDBC driver: A Java library that lets Pentaho and Tomcat connect to a specific database. Some drivers must be downloaded manually for licensing reasons and copied into Tomcat's lib directory, after which the server is restarted.
JNDI: Java Naming and Directory Interface, the mechanism Tomcat uses to expose named database connections. Pentaho references repository data sources by JNDI names that must stay consistent across Quartz, Hibernate, Jackrabbit, and Tomcat's context.xml.
Tomcat: The Apache servlet container that runs the Pentaho Server web application. Version 11 ships with Tomcat 10, which listens on port 8080 by default with a shutdown port of 8012.
PENTAHO_BASE: The environment variable identifying the root of the Pentaho install on Linux, typically /opt/pentaho. The labs set it in /etc/environment so install commands use consistent paths.
PENTAHO_JAVA_HOME: The environment variable that points Pentaho at the Java runtime it should use, set so the server consistently runs on Java 21.
OpenJDK: The free, open-source build of the Java platform under the GPL licence. Pentaho 11 requires Java 21, and the labs install OpenJDK 21 rather than Oracle JDK.
License Manager: The Pentaho Server administration screen used to apply and validate Enterprise Edition entitlements for PDI, BA, and the EE plugins. Licences are added by activation code or licensing URL.
EE licence: The Enterprise Edition entitlement that unlocks paid Pentaho features and plugins. The public download includes a 30-day trial licence valid on any supported OS.
Plugin: An add-on package that extends the Pentaho Server or PDI client with extra features such as reporting tools or new ETL steps. In version 11 big-data components and many features ship as plugins rather than being built in.
Plugin Manager: The built-in interface, available in both the modern PUC and the PDI client, for discovering, installing, updating, and removing server-side and client-side EE plugins.
Analyzer: An interactive, web-based analytics and visualisation tool for exploring OLAP data through drag-and-drop, drill-down, and pivot operations. It installs as the paz server plugin.
Interactive Reports: A web-based ad-hoc reporting tool, abbreviated PIR, that lets business users build tabular reports with grouping, filtering, and charts without SQL. It installs as the pir server plugin.
Dashboard Designer: A web-based tool for assembling interactive dashboards from charts, tables, and filters. It installs as the pdd server plugin.
Semantic Model Editor: A browser-based tool, abbreviated SME, introduced in version 11 for building and managing Mondrian data models, replacing the older Schema Workbench and Data Source Wizard workflow for many users.
Metadata Editor: The Pentaho Metadata Editor (PME) desktop client for creating business-friendly semantic models that sit between raw data and reports.
Schema Workbench: The Pentaho Schema Workbench (PSW) desktop client for creating and testing Mondrian OLAP cube schemas for multidimensional analysis.
Aggregation Designer: The Pentaho Aggregation Designer (PAD) desktop tool that recommends and builds aggregate tables to speed up Analyzer and OLAP queries.
OLAP: Online Analytical Processing, the multidimensional cube model that powers slice-and-dice, drill-down, and pivot analysis in tools such as Analyzer. Mondrian is Pentaho's OLAP engine.
Mondrian: Pentaho's OLAP engine, which executes multidimensional queries against schemas authored in Schema Workbench or the Semantic Model Editor.
Pentaho Upgrade Installer: The utility that backs up existing Pentaho products from version 8.3 or later and upgrades them in place to a newer release. It needs around 22 GB of free space and does not retain Hadoop drivers or plugins, which must be re-applied afterwards.
OIDC: OpenID Connect, an authentication standard supported in Pentaho 11 to enable single sign-on with identity providers such as Google, Okta, and Azure. It is offered alongside OAuth 2.0.
systemd: The Linux service manager used optionally in the labs to run the Pentaho Server at boot and restart it on failure, via a pentaho-server.service unit file.
